source.display_title: 05/26/2026 - Jorge Fernández  x Andrew Musial  — Lost

setter.evidence: No setter code in the title and none named on the call. The prospect came from an Instagram ad and did not know what the call was for: 'I don't know what I'm doing here. I don't know what this is, actually.'

prospect.name: Jorge Fernández
prospect.location: Mexican; travelling in Italy for a three-month trip, staying rent-free in his wife's aunt's house
prospect.occupation: Runs his own business — describes himself as a business guy who sells for a living: 'I understand the way this works, I do this for a living as well'
prospect.family_status: Married, travelling with his wife and two daughters aged three and one. Father is 75; father-in-law the same age and highly active.
prospect.training_background: Essentially none. Has never played a sport and has never sustained training — three attempts in his life, each abandoned within about two weeks (a high-school gym-and-nutritionist push, a bet with a friend using the Better Me app, and a restart after his first child was born). Currently three weeks into self-directed calisthenics from YouTube, plus whey protein and creatine started this week.

signals: Anchored to a free alternative he is actively using and finds is working — 'Right now, I'm doing it on YouTube' — and laid the comparison out feature by feature before concluding 'one of them is free. That's, I think, more amazing than the rest'
Self-directed and analytical: bought protein and creatine on his own research, doubled his own protein intake, set his own three-month target
Explicitly a value comparison rather than an inability to pay in principle — 'Knowing the trade-off I'm about, I'm giving up on, definitely'
Names himself as a peer in the sales conversation, which changes the register: 'I understand the way this works, I do this for a living as well'
Deviates from the pure type in that he genuinely had no cash — 'my current cash is zero' — so the bargain framing sits on top of a real liquidity floor

goals.text: Build muscle and get into good shape for the first time in his life, using the three-month trip as the window
Prove to himself that he can look better and be better — 'Look at myself in the mirror and say, hey, I can do this'
Start now at 34 because he believes every day of delay makes it harder — 'if I don't do it today, then tomorrow will be harder than yesterday'
Avoid ending up like his father, 75 and crippled, rather than like his equally aged father-in-law who trains
Be able to keep up with and set an example for two daughters aged three and one
Push back the age at which health problems start
Learn whether he is performing movements correctly — 'I have no idea if I did this push-up the right way or not'

pains.text: Has abandoned every training attempt of his life within about two weeks, three times over
Would genuinely rather watch television than train — 'I'd rather watch a TV series than work out, definitely'
Believes he has no time; works a lot and prefers to spend the rest with his family
No idea whether his self-taught form is correct and nobody to correct it
Has never gained weight despite eating freely — same weight since he was 15
Zero liquid cash; available funds are already committed to credit-card bills for the trip
Watching his father decline at 75 and fearing the same path

objections.rep_response: Ran the dinner comparison — 'If you would ask me for, take me out for a dinner, and it would be 6k, yeah, I would agree that that's a lot. But for a life-changing transformation, for life?'

objections.raw_quote: I don't think it's something I can afford.
objections.rep_response: Isolated it properly — 'finances aside, are you 100% sure that you can actually achieve your goals with Trevor?' and 'Is there anything else holding you back?' — then got permission for an open financial conversation and took cash, credit card and credit score.

objections.raw_quote: if we compare them, they're both at home. Amazing. They're both easy and quick. Amazing. They both give you more strength. Amazing. One of them also gives you the mobility and that sounds super amazing. One of them also has somebody that's following you up... But one of them is free. That's, I think, more amazing than the rest.
objections.rep_response: Conceded the content point — 'Everything, all the knowledge, everything, it's on YouTube. You can look it up' — then narrowed the differentiator to accountability and programming. The prospect agreed with the differentiator and still refused to pay for it.

objections.raw_quote: it's like, I don't know, wanting to starting to learn how to bike, and on the second, after two seconds, going and buying a mountain bike that's 6k. I would never do that. I would first go and buy a small, used bicycle... and then after a year, then I'll see if I'm prepared to spend 6k, but not now.
objections.rep_response: Agreed with the logic — 'Yeah, yeah, makes sense' — and moved directly to disqualifying: 'maybe it's not the time of the, not the right time in your life for these changes.'

offer.payment_plan_terms: No instalment structure was put forward. Rep said 'we don't have anything set in stone, like payment plans, but if there's a will, there's a way' and then offered third-party finance: 'one of the options is we have a financing partner.' The prospect declined at that ticket size.

prospect_financials.credit_score: self-described as amazing; answered '10' when asked
prospect_financials.note: Disclosed on the call: 'my current cash is zero... I have the exact cash I need to pay my credit cards that I which I've used to buy the tickets to fly to italy'. Uses credit cards. Number of cards, available credit and investments were never asked. Reference point for a meaningful spend was the $25 protein tub he had just bought.

evidence: Rep disqualified rather than continuing: 'maybe it's not the time of the, not the right time in your life for these changes'
Prospect refused at any framing: 'for 6k? No. Because it's not something I would ever pay 6k for'
Prospect confirmed the objection was priority as well as cash: 'it's definitely not something that's in my priorities of time and also of resources'
Prospect had pre-judged the outcome: 'I knew it was something that was gonna be difficult... but I suspected that was the case'
Call ended cleanly with no next step, no follow-up booked and no payment link
Counter-evidence: he agreed the offer would work — 'finances aside... definitely' — so this is lost on price and priority, not on belief
outcome.next_step: None. Both parties closed the call as no alignment.

notable.note: Cleanest disqualification in the batch and the sharpest articulation of the free-alternative problem: the prospect laid the offer side by side against free YouTube calisthenics, agreed with every claimed benefit including accountability, and still chose free. Two things a principal should see — he arrived not knowing what the call was ('I don't know what I'm doing here'), and after disclosing zero liquid cash and that his available funds were already committed to credit-card bills, he was offered a third-party financing partner.

quality.notes: Labels invert constantly, including a long unpunctuated block around 00:37:00 where both speakers are merged into one turn, and the daughters' ages ('Three and one') are attributed to the rep. Roles were read from content. The prospect's Fathom label carries a company suffix, 'Jorge Fernández - Tualo'.
